root.name: Latvian Gambit: Corkscrew Countergambit
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 f5 3. Bc4 fxe4 4. Nxe5 Nf6

overview: After 3.Bc4 fxe4 4.Nxe5 Nf6 material is level and White has Bxf7+ ideas, while Black has the half-open f-file. It is a countergambit with both sides setting traps around f7 and e4, and White usually gets the better game by sound development.

white_ideas.idea: Exploit the loose f7 with Bxf7+ or Nxf7 tactics

black_ideas.idea: Counterattack on e5 and e4 with ...d6 and ...Qe7

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with the e4 pawn on the board

character.notes: Unsure of the main line; read from the move order only.

gambit.notes: Material is level here, with Black's capture on e4 matching the pawn lost on e5.

soundness.notes: White has the easier game and the line is regarded as dubious for Black.

structure.notes: Pawns traded early leave open files.

approach.notes: A rare countergambit that strong players seldom choose.

level.notes: Mostly knowing the tactics after Bxf7+.

character.reason: Both kings are loose and the lines are tactical.

gambit.reason: Material is level at the root, so nothing is on offer in the main line.

soundness.reason: The Latvian family is generally thought to give White the better game.

structure.reason: The centre opens early with files and diagonals in play.

level.reason: A dubious line is never Beginner, and little theory is required.

plans.reason: Both sides revolve around the weak f7 square.
